With no output pasted it's a guess, but a crash right after install matches the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM case: @acme/cli has been ESM-only since PR #702, so an old Node fails. The reply will ask for `node -v` and the error text, and say to upgrade to Node 18+ and reinstall with `npm i -g @acme/cli`. For the startup check, it has to run before any ESM-only code loads, so it needs to be a tiny entry shim that checks the Node version and prints a colored warning, then imports the real CLI.
Action: draft the customer reply, add the version check shim (and an `engines` field, which was suggested but never added), and test it by simulating a low version.

My note says the team's Node is 18 LTS (from Aug 19), so I'll pin to major 18 unless you tell me it has changed. I'll add `.nvmrc` at the root and an `engines` field in the root package.json.

The common thread is that every error is a type imported with a regular import (ClientRow, Invoice, InvoiceFilters, FastifyPluginAsync and so on). With `verbatimModuleSyntax` on, types must be imported as `import type { X }` or `import { type X }` so the import can be erased exactly. It's mechanical, and an autofix can usually do it all.
Action: check which linter the repo uses and whether it has an import-type autofix rule, and if you want, run it and confirm typecheck is clean.

Most likely the token no longer reaches the request. With htmx the CSRF token has to be sent with the POST, either from a `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form or via an `X-CSRFToken` header (often set with `hx-headers` on body). Moving the form into a partial can break that, for instance if the partial is rendered without the request so the tag outputs nothing, or if the header lives on an element the partial no longer sits under.
Action: look at the partial and the view that renders it, check the posted request in dev tools for the token, and fix accordingly.

Put the trigger on the last card of each page: `hx-get` with the next page URL, `hx-trigger="revealed"`, `hx-swap="afterend"`, only when there is a next page, so it fires once as it scrolls into view and appends the next cards. If the list is in its own scrolling container rather than the window, use `intersect once` instead of `revealed`. Your view needs to return just the cards for HX-Request.
